title: SO/ Oxley Tower: a trophy home on Jalan Ampang.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #479 | SO/ OXLEY TOWER, KUALA LUMPUR
excerpt: The residential tower of a mixed development beside Four Seasons, steps from KLCC. Sean finds hotel-like common areas and a compact 711 sq ft unit, and calls it a trophy purchase rather than an investment.
takeaways: A discreet residential tower beside an office tower and a hotel, steps from KLCC.
A 711 sq ft unit lists at about RM1.5 to RM1.6 million; KLCC-facing units ask up to about RM3,000 psf.
Rent of about RM7,500 to RM8,000 roughly breaks even, so Sean sees it as a trophy, not an investment.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Oxley Tower splits its uses into three towers, an office, a hotel and the SO/ residences, over shared retail and basement car parks. The 77-storey residential tower has its own discreet entrance, six lifts serving 12 units a floor, and lift lobbies and corridors finished and fully air-conditioned like a hotel, with no voids. Management has banned Airbnb.

Sean viewed a 711 sq ft unit with one bedroom plus a small study, a storeroom, De Dietrich kitchen appliances, a large bathroom shared by the bedroom and guests, and full-height glass that shuts out the street noise. Half of level 46 is a gym, beside one of the biggest yoga rooms he has seen, and the rooftop has a lap pool and a children's playground.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It is on Jalan Ampang beside Four Seasons and next to Wisma Central, a short walk from KLCC, Avenue K and several LRT and MRT stations, with tree-shaded walkways and new bus lanes. Street food, local shops, the park, galleries and the aquarium are all on foot. Old buildings around it are being torn down and rebuilt, including a hotel next door.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: On a listings site, units facing KLCC ask about RM2,800 to RM3,000 psf and those facing elsewhere about RM1,800 to RM2,000 psf, putting this unit at about RM1.5 to RM1.6 million. Furnished units like it ask about RM7,500 to RM8,000 a month, and Sean reckons even RM7,000 would only about break even. He sees it suiting a well-paid couple who work nearby.

standout.title: A front door you'd walk past
standout.body: The offices and shops take the street frontage, and the residences' entrance is tucked to one side, so discreet that Sean struggled to find it. Inside, an intimate lobby leads to hotel-style lift lobbies and corridors, a calm contrast to the busy street outside.

pros: The location is unbeatable: everyone else measures their commute to KLCC, the highways end around its fringe, transit and walkways are excellent, and alongside the luxury malls there are local shops, street food, parks and the aquarium within walking distance.

The architecture: three towers separated by use over shared parking and retail, a discreet entrance and hotel-like common areas, good soundproofing, a generous bathroom, a gym on half a floor and one of the biggest yoga rooms he has seen. The rooftop isn't the best KLCC view, but it has perhaps the country's highest children's playground.

It is a trophy: bought to mark success rather than for own stay or yield, since RM7,000 in rent roughly breaks even. It suits a high-earning couple who walk to work, and the ban on Airbnb protects its exclusivity.
cons: The micro location: the left turn in beside Wisma Central is narrowed by illegal parking and lunchtime food trucks, peak-hour traffic is heavy, and demolition and construction around it are noisy until you shut the windows.

Below his expectations after Four Seasons: the facilities don't wow, the corridor is almost too dark, the three end units' doors face each other, the mixed-use car park is confusing and the small residential floor plate stacks the facilities over separate floors. In the unit, the study has no window, the shared bathroom has two doors and the kitchen is small.
Constant redevelopment: the city skyline keeps changing, so no view except the one from the pool is certain, and more branded residences are on the way.

closing: A trophy property for buyers who want a KLCC address to call their own, not a home bought for its rental yield.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this November 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view a furnished investment unit; prices and rents are asking figures from a listings site as he quoted them.
